### The idiom — 15 rules, each grounded in parse-that's own source/parsers
Highlights the candidates cannot invent around: regex is a **terminal only** (default `regex()` returns the whole match — capture groups are unreachable); **`all()` drops `undefined` arms at runtime** while TS keeps the position, so `.opt()` must never go inside `all()` (use `.then()`); arity lives in `sepBy(sep,min,max)`; `Parser.lazy` once per **back-edge**, not per production; precedence is written as a climb, **never** left-recursive; entry point is `parseState()`+`isError`, never `parse()`; error caret is `state.furthest`, and `state.expected` is empty unless `enableDiagnostics()`.

### The `skip` caveat — VERDICT
**REAL, reproduces exactly** (`string("a").skip(string("b")).parseState("ax")` → `isError:true, offset:0, value:"a"`). **NOT a `skip` defect** — `then`/`next`/`all`/`wrap` are identical; it is the library's uniform error-path discipline (`value` is undefined-by-contract when `isError`), and `.opt()` is the sole scrubbing combinator. **The hazard is `Parser.parse()`**, which is `parseState(val).value` with no `isError` consult: `regex(/[a-z]+/).skip(string("(")).skip(string(")")).parse("oklch(")` returns `"oklch"` — **the R1 bug reconstituted in the new library**. Classification: **misuse, not defect**; cure is one line. Nothing filed upstream — 1.0.0 is the contract.

### Anti-patterns — executable, not prose
AP-1 hand-rolled cursor (transcribed `splitTopLevel` → `[]` on empty body → caller's `slash[0]!.replace` throws `TypeError`; the R1 crash reproduced **from the technique**, not imported) · AP-2 regex-as-parser (groups unreachable; `matchFunction` returning `""` = success/no-value/**zero-width**) · AP-3 broad remainder (`.*` rejects valid `rgb(1,2,3)`; `[^)]*` truncates nesting) · AP-4 `chain` where `map` suffices (factory-call counter) · AP-5 god-production · AP-6 imperative balanced scan · AP-7 `parse()`-truthiness · AP-8 decorative `memoize()`.

### Two findings worth escalating to the band
1. **`memoize()` is not locally scoped.** Constructing *any* memoized wrapper sets `PACKRAT_ARMED = true` **process-wide and it never disarms** (`packrat.ts` → `makeMemoized`). One decorative `memoize()` in a colour parser makes **every** top-level `parseState()` in value.js pay an epoch snapshot/restore. Ruling for the band: **no packrat in the CSS grammar.**
2. **The `all()` drop-`undefined` trap is live in parse-that's own test suite.** `test/math.test.ts:18-22` emits the string `"e2undefined"` for input `"e2"`; the suite is green only because `parseFloat` stops at the first invalid char. Pinned as evidence about published semantics, **not** as an upstream change request.

## Surface — one prior record corrected

`./css` = **52 symbols CONFIRMED** (19 values + 33 types). Measured three independent ways that agree: TS AST over `src/subpaths/*.ts`, regex cross-check, and the `.d.ts` rollups inside `npm pack @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0`.

**The package total is 141 distinct names, NOT 126.** `./transform` contributes exactly 15 and `141 − 15 = 126`; no other subpath subset fits, and no reachable commit yields 126. Recorded as the only consistent explanation, not as proven. Also found: pre-`164343c1` the map was `./parsing`/`./units` with **337** names — the v4 cut was 337 → 141 (−58%), and npm serves the new map, so tree and published artifact agree.

## R1 is far worse than eight strings

- **Unbounded input class**, not 8 inputs: `parseCssColor` throws for every `/^[a-z][\w-]*\([\s\/]*\)$/i` minus six guarded heads (`var env hsv kelvin ictcp jzazbz`). `hwb()` `rgba()` `hsla()` `xyz()` `calc()` `url()` `rgb(/)` `rgb(\t)` and **`foo()`** — any unknown function — all throw. Asserted exhaustively over a generated 21×10 = 210-member sub-language plus a negative predicate test.
- **6 of the 10 public entries throw**, not one: `parseCssColor`, `parseCssScalar`, `parseCssValue`, `parseCssValues`, `parseStylesheet`, `coerceToSyntax` — because `parseScalarInternal` calls `parseCssColor` first for every scalar. `parseStylesheet("a{color:rgb()}")` throws.
- **Four new unsound accepts found**: `rgb(1 2 3 / )` / `rgb(1,2,3,)` → opaque (P-037); `calc(1px + )` `calc(*)` `calc(+)` accept (P-046); `pow(2)` `clamp(1px)` accept (P-047); `animation-range: 1s` accepts (P-066).

## The scoreboard — 83 numbered productions, 325 probes

`SHIPS 54 · DEFERRED 3 · GAP 18 · UNSOUND 4 · CRASH 4`
Tier 1 = 57 (52 SHIPS, 1 UNSOUND, 4 CRASH) · tier 2 = 18 · tier 3 = 8.

Tier-2 gaps that matter: legacy `rgba(r,g,b,a)`/`hsla(...)` (P-012/P-015 — the most-deployed colour syntax on the web), `color-mix()` (P-028 — `mixColors` already ships on `./color`, only syntax missing), `light-dark()`, unquoted `url()`, single-stop `linear()`, and 3 of 7 `<timeline-range-name>`s refused as keyframe selectors while accepted in `animation-range`.

Two findings in the other direction: **value.js's 148 named colours are name-for-name identical to the css-color-4 table** (zero misses, zero extras, asserted over 148×3 spellings); and **`@scroll-timeline`/`@view-timeline` at-rules were removed from scroll-animations-1** — value.js models both and exports 2 types for them (P-074, obsolete surface).

`grammar.ts` measures **72 non-null assertions, 70 of them index-access** by AST (the brief's "70 index-`!`" is exact; "74" measures 72). `src/css/` totals 1888 lines / 94 non-null / 86 index.

## Posture

No benchmark run, no speed claim — the prior gate measured the regex as fastest and I did not relitigate it. The case rests on 4 crash sites over an unbounded class, 4 unsound accepts, 18 named gaps, and 86 `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` overrides. Against that, **52 tier-1 productions ship correctly and must not regress** — the test fails the build if any tier-1 production other than the five already-broken ones leaves SHIPS.

### Headline findings

**1. The mirror runs FOUR tests.** One file, all four the G16 tests. `npm test`'s config also includes `cells/**/test/**` — which matches **0 of 557 files** (zero `test/` dirs exist there). `npm run check` uses `tsconfig.apotheosis.json`, which *excludes* the 10,073 lines of pre-reset parser; `check:rejected-g0` on that code reports 19 errors. The green is green because it was scoped down.

**2. The 180 sealed cases are permanently undecryptable.** Nine AES-256-GCM ciphertexts (1.5 MiB); `g14/holdout-recovery-reveal.json` records `original_key_continuity: false` ("turn-local custodian key store expired"). Zero key/escrow material anywhere in 2,349 files; several holdouts explicitly destroyed. **V·π's central correctness claim — "180 of 180 pass", 65,024 oracle transactions — is not disputed, it is unopenable.** The one survivor is `value-percentage-literal/g0`, which wrote literal data instead of a hash commitment.

**3. G16 verdict: ADAPT.** It *is* idiomatic — scored against GROUND-B's own §6 checklist it passes every applicable rule (one-token regex, no capture-group structure, zero `!`, module-level const). And I re-established correctness independently since V·π's evidence can't be reopened: **49/49 prefix cases** (entering at recorded non-zero offsets via `new ParserState(src,undefined,offset)`), **11/11 hostile no-throw**, 7/7 generated 32K/1M-unit inputs, stable parser id, transactional failure. Not start-clean (it's measured-correct). Not adopt-as-is: it silently imports two undecided contracts — it discards source spelling (`"1.0"`→`value:1`, but `<dimension>` needs the spelling to round-trip) and `value: number` admits `±Infinity`. Both pinned as tests. No speed claim made; timings only establish absence of catastrophic backtracking.

**4. The integrity tests caught a real error on first run** — I had transcribed `-7x` as `value: 7`. Same failure class as the known-dimensions kill in miniature.

**5. Best salvage: the identifier-boundary counterexample.** Three candidates passed 1,131 green transactions; **all three were wrong**. The bank tested `1px\78` but omitted both discriminating cases. `1px\` at EOF must *fail* (escape-to-EOF → U+FFFD → unit is `px�`); `1px\`+LF/CRLF/CR/FF must *succeed through* `px`. H/S under-reject, B over-rejects. Reviewers' repair: consume the canonical identifier production, never invent a boundary regex.

**6. R6 and R9 are traps for differential harnesses.** R6 is a *value* divergence (both accept `hsl(120 50 50)`; 50 vs 0.5) — an `ok`-only differential misses it. R9 is bidirectional (LIVE both over- and under-accepts). R2/R5/R7/R12 have no executable fixtures — V·π waves W4/W5 were never authored; stated honestly in the corpus.
